chains.title: FOXA1-dependent regulation of TOX3
chains.element: A CASC16 intronic site 38 bp from a dELS element; the dELS does not overlap the variant, and its reported activity maxima are not MCF-7-specific.

links.claim: FOXA1 is a leading candidate because it has multiple MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks over the variant and is highly expressed; literature also mentions altered FOXA1 affinity in a TOX3 enhancer context. The ref-G direction is only a testable working hypothesis: no QBiC-SELEX result or other allele-specific binding evidence is supplied for this variant.
The variant lies in a CASC16 intron and near, but not within, an annotated dELS; the available activity maxima do not establish activity in MCF-7 or a variant-dependent effect.

TOX3 is the nearest listed protein-coding gene, and a literature quote describes a FOXA1-affinity/TOX3 enhancer hypothesis at a masked locus; neither establishes that this variant or nearby dELS regulates TOX3, and no significant GTEx eQTL is reported.
FOXA1 occupancy over the variant and high FOXA1 expression are reported in MCF-7, making it a relevant context in which to test this chain.

TOX3 has breast-cancer association evidence, but no evidence here connects this variant to TOX3 expression or disease; TOX3 is not a CRISPR dependency in MCF7, which provides no support for an essential-growth mechanism.

predictions: Allele-resolved FOXA1 occupancy in MCF-7 will be higher on ref G than alt A; this direction is a hypothesis, not an evidence-based prediction.
If the site affects TOX3 through FOXA1, perturbing FOXA1 will alter the relevant regulatory output and TOX3 expression more than perturbing GATA3.
falsified_if: A sufficiently powered allele-resolved assay finds no FOXA1 occupancy imbalance or finds higher occupancy on alt A.
FOXA1 perturbation has no effect on the candidate regulatory output or TOX3 expression in a relevant assay.
